item.text:
**Gap 1 is unproved. Gap 2 is unproved. The whole argument does not close.** If both gaps were established, the numerical estimates and the application of the one-sided criterion would give the target for the usual pole-removed entire \(L\)-function.

### Gap 1 — Unproved

The first obstruction is that the sketch does not define an admissible geometric datum or specify the lattice in which the short lifts are to be constructed. In particular, it gives no lift length bound, index bound, or covolume estimates with a common height term. The formulas for \(\mathcal B\) and \(\mathrm{rem}\) define the quantities in the desired inequality but give no relation between them. The asserted height cancellation therefore cannot be checked from the allowed facts.

### Gap 2 — Unproved

The first obstruction is again the missing definition of admissibility. There is no construction to check for each positive multiple \(M\) of \(18480\), each prime \(d\) with \(M\mid 2(d+1)\) and \(M\nmid d+1\), and each \(0<\varepsilon<1/100\), for every sufficiently large \(x\).

The last estimate also has an independent missing step. The sketch supplies no transform identities or bounds from which to deduce that some \(\log x_1\) in the stated interval satisfies
\[
R_M(x_1)-\frac TH R_1(x_1)\le x^{-10^6}
\]
with \(T/H\) coming from the same admissible datum as the bounds on \(m\), \(b\), and \(f/H\). The allowed facts give no small-value estimate of this kind.

### Conditional check of the endgame

Fix \(q,\chi,\rho\) in the target, outside the stated exception, and put \(\sigma=\Re\rho\). For \(M=18480q\) and \(a=M/2-1\), we have \(a\equiv7\pmod 8\) and \(\gcd(a,M)=1\), since \(a\) is odd and \(M=2(a+1)\). Every prime \(d\equiv a\pmod M\) is therefore \(7\bmod 8\) and coprime to \(M\). Also \(d+1\equiv M/2\pmod M\), which gives both divisibility hypotheses of the gaps. The chosen \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(0<\varepsilon\le 1/102<1/100\), and
\[
0<8\varepsilon=\frac8{51}\bigl(\min(\sigma,1)-1/2\bigr)<\sigma-1/2.
\]
Thus \(1/2<\beta<\sigma\).

Assume both gaps and fix any such prime \(d\). For every sufficiently large \(x\), use the datum from Gap 2 in Gap 1. Dividing by \(mAH>0\), with \(A\) a positive order, gives
\[
R_M(x)\le \frac{f(\log b)^5}{mH}+x^{-10^6}
\le \varphi(M)x^{6\varepsilon-1/2}+x^{-10^6}.
\]
The ratio of the final upper bound to \(x^{8\varepsilon-1/2}\) is
\[
\varphi(M)x^{-2\varepsilon}+x^{-10^6+1/2-8\varepsilon},
\]
which tends to zero for fixed \(M,\varepsilon\). Hence \(R_M(x)\le x^{\beta-1}\) eventually for each such \(d\). The criterion permits the eventual threshold to depend on \(d\).

The criterion would then give nonvanishing at \(\rho\) for the entire function of the character induced to modulus \(M\). With the usual normalization, this is the ordinary \(L\)-function for a nonprincipal character and the ordinary \(L\)-function multiplied by \(s-1\) for a principal character. The latter multiplier is nonzero at every point in the principal case covered by the target. Induction preserves principality in both directions because reduction of unit groups from modulo \(M\) to modulo \(q\) is surjective. Finally,
\[
L(s,\chi_M)=L(s,\chi)\prod_{\substack{p\mid M\\p\nmid q}}
(1-\chi(p)p^{-s}).
\]
Every displayed factor is nonzero at \(\rho\), since \(|\chi(p)p^{-\rho}|=p^{-\sigma}<1\). This would transfer nonvanishing to \(L(\rho,\chi)\). The eventual prime-error bound needed to invoke the criterion remains unproved.
